sections.title: Turning a noun into a description
sections.content: Adding -s (or -as/-es/-os by vowel harmony) to a noun makes an adjective meaning "having that thing" — szemüveg ("glasses") becomes szemüveges ("wearing glasses"), szakáll ("beard") becomes szakállas ("bearded"). It's a productive pattern: once you spot it, you can guess plenty of new -s adjectives yourself.

items.english: My neighbor is bearded and wears glasses.

items.spanish: Milyen a kollégád? Magas és szemüveges.
items.english: What's your colleague like? Tall and wearing glasses.

sections.content: This is exactly the same job -i does for adjectives elsewhere (like heti from hét in Unit 2) — Hungarian has more than one way to turn a noun into a describing word, and -s is the one for "has this feature".
